questions.question_text:
A continuous random variable has $f(x) = \dfrac{3x^{2}}{26}$ on $[1,3]$, and $0$ elsewhere.
Find its cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ for $1 \le x \le 3$.

options.why: Never substitutes the lower limit $t = 1$, so $F(1)$ does not come out as $0$.
After correctly integrating to $\dfrac{t^{3}}{26}$, divides by $3$ again, giving the incorrect denominator $78$.
Both slips together: the extra division by $3$ and the missing lower limit.

questions.question_text:
A continuous random variable has $f(x) = \dfrac{2e^{2x}}{e^{6} - 1}$ on $[0,3]$, and $0$ elsewhere.
Find its cumulative distribution function $F(x)$.

options.why: Never substitutes the lower limit $t = 0$, so the $-1$ from $e^{0}$ is missing.
Keeps the factor $2$ instead of cancelling it against the $\frac{1}{2}$ from integrating $e^{2t}$.
Both slips together: the leftover factor $2$ and the missing lower limit.

questions.question_text:
A continuous random variable has cumulative distribution function $F(x) = \dfrac{x^{4} - 1}{624}$ on $[1,5]$.
Find $P(2 \le X \le 3)$.

options.why: Adds $F(3)$ and $F(2)$ instead of subtracting them.
Gives the complement, $1 - \left(F(3) - F(2)\right)$, which is the probability outside the interval.
Both slips together: the two values are added and then the complement is taken.

questions.question_text:
A continuous random variable has cumulative distribution function $F(x) = \dfrac{x^{3} + 8}{16}$ on $[-2,2]$.
Find its probability density function $f(x)$.

options.why: Differentiates the $x^{3}$ term but carries the constant $8$ through unchanged.
Drops the factor $3$ that comes from differentiating $x^{3}$.
Integrates $F$ instead of differentiating it.

questions.question_text:
A continuous random variable has cumulative distribution function $F(x) = \dfrac{x^{2} - 4}{60}$ on $[2,8]$.
Find $P(3 \le X \le 6)$.

options.why: Uses only $F(6) = \dfrac{32}{60}$, so includes the probability below $3$.
Adds $F(6) = \dfrac{32}{60}$ and $F(3) = \dfrac{5}{60}$ instead of subtracting them.
Takes the complement of the interval probability, giving $1 - \dfrac{9}{20}$.

questions.question_text:
A continuous random variable has cumulative distribution function $F(x) = \dfrac{x^{2} - 9}{40}$ on $[3,7]$.
Find $P(X > 5)$.

options.why: Gives $F(5) = P(X \le 5)$, the probability on the wrong side of $5$.
Drops the $-9$ from $F$, using $\frac{25}{40}$ as the value of $F(5)$.
Both slips together: the $-9$ is dropped and the wrong side of $5$ is taken.
Incorrectly applies the second density height $0.3$ from $x = 0$, calculating $\int_{0}^{x}0.3\,dt = 0.3x$.
Calculates $0.3(x - 2)$ but omits the accumulated probability $0.4$.
Incorrectly uses $0.2$ as the slope and adds the density height $0.3$ as a constant.

questions.question_text:
A continuous random variable defined on $[0,20]$ has cumulative distribution function $F$, with $F(6) = 0.28$ and $F(14) = 0.73$.
Find the probability that $X$ lies outside the interval from $6$ to $14$.

options.why: Gives $F(14) - F(6)$, the probability inside the interval rather than outside it.
Adds the two cumulative values, which double-counts the probability below $6$.
